nodes.content: Investigate causal effect identifiability reasoning from diagrams, distinguishing structural edits from equivalent redrawings across unseen graph compositions.
requirements: Achieve 85% paired accuracy on identifiability judgments before and after structural edits, including latent confounding.
Maintain 95% prediction consistency across equivalent redrawings of held-out graph compositions.

nodes.content: Parse diagrams into directed-bidirected graphs; train a permutation-invariant model with ID-algorithm labels, paired edit supervision, and redrawing-consistency loss.
Can bidirected-edge encoding preserve identifiability judgments under redrawings while detecting latent-confounding edits in unseen graph compositions?
Permutation-invariant bidirected graph encoding with paired-edit and redraw losses achieves ≥85% paired accuracy and ≥95% consistency on held-out compositions.
Generate ID-labeled composition splits with directed and latent-edge edits plus equivalent redrawings; train encoder and assess both metrics.
Train bidirected encoder on 8,000 ID-labeled graphs; measure paired accuracy and redrawing consistency across 1,000 held-out compositions, including latent-edge edits.
On 1,000 held-out compositions, paired accuracy reached 88% (86% on latent-edge edits), and equivalent-redrawing consistency reached 97%.
Adopt the bidirected encoder as the baseline: 88% paired accuracy and 97% redrawing consistency exceed both targets.
Release CausalEdit-ID v1 with ID-labeled composition splits, structural-edit pairs, equivalent redrawings, and bidirected-encoder evaluation scripts.
Using the adopted baseline and CausalEdit-ID v1, measure paired accuracy and redrawing consistency on 400 unseen two-latent-edge edit compositions.
On 400 unseen two-latent-edge compositions, paired accuracy fell to 79%, below 85%, despite 96% redrawing consistency.
Adding ID-algorithm district-decomposition supervision will raise two-latent-edge paired accuracy from 79% to ≥85% without reducing redraw consistency below 95%.
Annotate ID districts, retrain with district-decomposition loss, then compare paired accuracy and redraw consistency on the fixed two-latent-edge holdout.
Augment CausalEdit-ID v1 with ID district labels; retrain the encoder and score both metrics on the fixed 400-composition holdout.
District supervision raised two-latent-edge paired accuracy from 79% to 83%, below 85%; redrawing consistency remained 96%.
Using CausalEdit-ID v1, sweep district-loss weights (0.1–1.0) and rescore paired accuracy and redraw consistency on the 400-composition holdout.
At district-loss weight 0.4, paired accuracy reached 86% versus 79% baseline; redrawing consistency held at 96%.
Weight-0.4 district supervision, unlike untuned training, will maintain ≥85% paired accuracy and ≥95% redraw consistency on fresh two-latent-edge compositions.
Freeze weight-0.4 encoder, generate an independent two-latent-edge composition set, and evaluate paired accuracy and redrawing consistency without retuning.
Using CausalEdit-ID v1 scripts, score the frozen weight-0.4 encoder on 600 independent two-latent-edge edit pairs and redrawings.
On 600 independent two-latent-edge edit pairs, paired accuracy was 86% and equivalent-redrawing consistency was 96%.
Release CausalEdit-ID v2 with 600 independent two-latent-edge test pairs, redrawings, frozen weight-0.4 encoder, and metric scripts.
Using CausalEdit-ID v2’s frozen encoder and scripts, score 500 fresh two-latent-edge edit pairs and equivalent redrawings.
On 500 fresh two-latent-edge edit pairs, paired accuracy fell to 82%, below 85%, while redrawing consistency remained 96%.
Use canonical ADMG parsing with edge-edit supervision and exact ID-algorithm execution instead of direct identifiability prediction.
Can canonical ADMG parsing distinguish latent-edge edits from redrawings reliably enough for exact ID execution on unseen compositions?
Train an ADMG parser on paired edits and redrawings; validate extracted edges, then run exact ID across held-out compositions.
Train an edit-supervised ADMG parser on CausalEdit-ID v1; measure edge accuracy, exact-ID paired accuracy, and redraw consistency on v2.
On CausalEdit-ID v2, parser edge F1 reached 97%; exact-ID paired accuracy reached 89% and redrawing consistency 98%.
Release ADMG-ID pipeline v1 with the edit-supervised parser, canonical graph serializer, exact ID executor, and v2 evaluation script.
Use query-conditioned causal-motif retrieval and edit-localized reasoning, matching isomorphic redrawings before recomputing identifiability after latent-edge changes.
Can query-conditioned motif retrieval generalize to unseen compositions without mistaking latent-edge edits for isomorphic redrawings?
Query-conditioned motif retrieval with edit localization achieves ≥85% paired accuracy and ≥95% redraw consistency on unseen latent-edge compositions.
Using ADMG-ID pipeline v1 labels, measure edit-localized motif retrieval’s paired accuracy and redraw consistency on 500 unseen latent-edge compositions.
Paired accuracy reached 86% and redraw consistency 96%; 24% of identifiability-flipping latent edits were incorrectly cached as redrawings.
Using ADMG-ID pipeline v1, evaluate motif retrieval on 600 fresh latent-edge compositions for paired accuracy, redraw consistency, and flip-cache errors.
On 600 fresh compositions, paired accuracy dropped to 81%, below 85%; redraw consistency held at 96%, with 28% flip-cache errors.
Canonical bidirected-edge checks before motif-cache reuse will cut flip-cache errors below 10%, yielding ≥85% paired accuracy and ≥95% redraw consistency.
Gate motif-cache reuse on query-preserving canonical ADMG equality; remeasure flip-cache errors, paired accuracy, and redraw consistency on fresh compositions.
Implement a query-preserving canonical ADMG cache gate using pipeline v1; measure flip-cache errors, paired accuracy, and redraw consistency.
On 600 fresh compositions, canonical gating cut flip-cache errors from 28% to 7%; paired accuracy reached 87%, redraw consistency 97%.
Release MotifGate v1 with query-preserving canonical ADMG cache checks, flip-cache error auditing, and paired-accuracy evaluation scripts.
Adopt canonical-gated retrieval: paired accuracy rose from 81% to 87%, flip-cache errors dropped to 7%, and redrawing consistency reached 97%.
Use parser ensembles and ID-algorithm certificates to target uncertain latent edges for verification before judging canonicalized diagrams.
Can certificate-guided verification of parser-disputed latent edges improve paired judgments without disrupting equivalent-redrawing consistency?
Ensemble-parse 600 held-out compositions; verify disputed certificate-critical bidirected edges, then compare paired accuracy and redraw consistency with ADMG-ID v1.
Extend MotifGate v1 with three-parser checks of certificate-critical latent edges; compare paired accuracy and redraw consistency against baseline.
On 600 held-out compositions, certificate-guided verification raised paired accuracy from 87% to 91%; redraw consistency remained 97%.
Release CertGate v1, adding three-parser latent-edge disagreement checks and ID-certificate verification to MotifGate v1.
Using CertGate v1, compare paired accuracy and redraw consistency against MotifGate on 500 fresh three-latent-edge compositions.
On 500 fresh three-latent-edge compositions, CertGate paired accuracy fell to 82% versus MotifGate’s 86%; redrawing consistency stayed 97%.
Defer CertGate adoption: initial paired accuracy rose to 91%, but fresh three-latent-edge accuracy fell to 82% versus MotifGate’s 86%.
Use ID-disagreement-guided counterexample synthesis to train parsers on three-latent-edge edits, with canonical ADMG augmentation for redraw invariance.
Can ID-disagreement counterexamples correct three-latent-edge edit failures while preserving redraw invariance on unseen graph compositions?
ID-disagreement counterexample training yields ≥85% three-latent-edge paired accuracy and ≥95% redrawing consistency on unseen compositions.
Extend CertGate v1: synthesize 2,000 ID-disagreement edits, retrain with redrawings, evaluate paired accuracy and consistency on 500 unseen three-latent-edge compositions.
On 500 unseen three-latent-edge compositions, counterexample-trained CertGate achieved 88% paired accuracy and 97% redrawing consistency.
Using CertGate v1, ablate counterexample training on 600 fresh three-latent-edge compositions; compare paired accuracy and redrawing consistency.
On 600 fresh compositions, counterexample-trained CertGate reached 86% paired accuracy and 96% redraw consistency; ablated CertGate reached 88% and 97%.
Defer counterexample training: initial paired accuracy was 88%, but fresh testing yielded 86% versus 88% without it.
Verified ID-flip counterexamples with balanced redrawings will exceed ablated CertGate’s 88% paired accuracy on fresh three-latent-edge compositions, retaining ≥95% consistency.
Verify synthetic ID flips, balance redrawings, retrain CertGate, and compare paired accuracy against the 88% ablation on fresh compositions.
CertGate v1: verify ID-flip counterexamples, balance redrawings, retrain, and measure paired accuracy and redraw consistency on 600 fresh three-latent-edge compositions.
On 600 fresh three-latent-edge compositions, verified-counterexample CertGate achieved 90% paired accuracy and 97% redrawing consistency.
With CertGate v1, compare verified-flip training against the 88% ablation on 800 independent three-latent-edge compositions and redrawings.
On 800 independent compositions, verified-flip CertGate achieved 87% paired accuracy versus the ablation’s 88%, with 97% redrawing consistency.
Stratify 700 fresh three-latent-edge compositions by district overlap; compare verified-flip CertGate with ablation on paired accuracy and redraw consistency.
Across 700 fresh district-stratified compositions, verified-flip CertGate reached 90% paired accuracy versus ablation’s 87%; redraw consistency was 97%.
Using CertGate v1, compare verified-flip training against ablation on 900 parser-disagreement-stratified three-latent-edge compositions; measure paired accuracy and redraw consistency.
On 900 parser-disagreement-stratified compositions, verified-flip CertGate scored 83% paired accuracy, below 85%, while redraw consistency stayed 97%.
Defer deployment: initial and district-stratified accuracy reached 90%, but independent accuracy trailed ablation 87%–88%, and parser-disagreement accuracy fell to 83%.
